newsitem.title: GERMANY: German budget woes should not delay EMU - Rexrodt.
newsitem.headline: German budget woes should not delay EMU - Rexrodt.

text.p: German Economics Minister Gunter Rexrodt said on Monday that European monetary union should not be delayed because of Bonn's budget problems, because that would be economically damaging and politically shortsighted.

"I see the current delay debate as dangerous in economic and political terms," he said in a statement. "Credibility and reliability as well as the political will to grow together further would be damaged."
A delay in the planned 1999 start of EMU would put the single currency at risk and raise questions about far-reaching integration goals, he said.
A delay would also drive speculative buying of the mark, raising its value and making German exports more expensive, Rexrodt said. "This would hinder foreign trade and cost jobs."
Pushing back the start of EMU could also destabilise exchange rates, interest rates and inflation, he warned.
"The euro means more than savings on transaction costs," Rexrodt said. "It has to do with the economic and political future of Germany and Europe."
